This Criminal Petition, coming on for orders, this day, the court made the following:

ORDER Sri Diwakar Maddur, HCGP, takes notice for respondent No.1.
2.

The allegations made in the charge sheet are that the petitioner promised the second respondent to marry her and in the background of this false promise, on 14.3.2019 at 7.00 pm the petitioner had sexual intercourse against her will at a resort by name Mookanana, Sakleshpura, Hassan District.

On 18.3.2019 in between 7.00 and 7.30 am, second respondent went to the house of the petitioner at Chandra Layout, Bengaluru, to question him about the incident dated 14.3.2019 and at that time also the petitioner promised the second respondent to marry her and again had sexual intercourse NC: 2023:KHC:45798 with her against her will.

It is also stated that on 11.09.2019 in between 12.30 and 3.00 am, the petitioner had sexual intercourse with the second respondent against her will under a promise of marriage, as a result the second respondent became pregnant.
The pregnancy was terminated.
In the charge sheet petitioner is accused no.1.
Accused No.2 was Dr. Shilpa.
The charge sheet against accused no.2 was quashed by order dated 10.12.2021 in Criminal Petition 2964/2021.
3. The second respondent, namely Jyothi H is present before the court.
She unequivocally submits that she has withdrawn all the allegations made against the petitioner and has no objection for quashing the charge sheet.

4. From the charge sheet allegations it can be seen that second respondent had been married to CW16 and the submission of the second respondent now is that marriage was dissolved in the month of September 2019 by an order of the Family Court, Davanagere.

That means NC:
2023:KHC:45798 on the first date of alleged forcible sexual intercourse i.e. 14.03.2019, she was married and the question of making a promise by the petitioner to marry her cannot be imagined.
In the facts and circumstances, I also do not find that there exists any material to invoke the provisions of the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act.

sentences.text: Be that as it may.

Since the second respondent has withdrawn all the allegations made against the petitioner and has no objection for quashing the charge sheet, this court can exercise power under section 482 Cr.P.C for quashing the charge sheet.
Sri P.Prasanna Kumar relies on two orders passed by the coordinate bench in Criminal Petitions 12353/2023 and 12378/2023 between the same parties.
In these two cases the offences invoked were punishable under sections 341, 506 and 448 of IPC.

The allegations B L Channaveeresh vs State Of Karnataka on 15 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/61970469/
2 were that the petitioner forced the second respondent to withdraw all the cases against him and say no objection for quashing the proceedings.

sentences.text: In these two cases respondent no.2 appeared before the coordinate bench and said no NC: 2023:KHC:45798 objection.
In this background what figures out is that probably the second respondent might have made false allegations against the petitioner.
The whole act of sexual intercourse appears to consensual one.

If the petitioner is asked to face the trial,
it is a futile exercise.
The allegations made in the charge sheet do not constitute any offence which requires a trial to be held.
Hence, the petition is allowed.

The proceedings in Spl. C. no. 728/2020 on the file of LXX Additional City Civil and Sessions Judge and Special Judge, Bengaluru (CCH-71),
are quashed.
